function: Excluded (system): over-the-air FL aggregation (precoding plus Bayesian MMSE aggregation at the server) over a MAC with single-antenna users and server, no RIS; p. 4, p. 11.
notes: Reason system (Step 1 code 6), area 7 work with single-antenna links and no RIS. p. 4: "each user of index i experiences at round r a block fading channel h_i^r e^{j phi_i^r}, where h_i^r > 0 and e^{j phi_i^r} ... are its magnitude and phase"; the server receives y^r = sum_i h_i^r x_i^r + w^r (Eq. 6), one scalar coefficient per user, where the d x 1 vector is the model sent over d channel uses, not an antenna array. p. 11: "block fading channel coefficients h_i^r are sampled from a Rayleigh distribution in an i.i.d. fashion" and "Future work could explore the impact of multi-antenna systems on our Bayesian aggregation and control variates approach for OTA FL". No MIMO, antenna array, beamforming, or RIS appears anywhere in the text. Earlier codes do not apply: IEEE TSP research article (p. 1); it proposes and evaluates BAAF and COBAAF, not a survey (p. 1); OTA FL passes no_learning; the aggregation is analog over-the-air computation over the MAC (p. 2: "the users transmit their model updates via analog signalling"), so it is physical layer and the problem it solves is the OTA aggregation itself, area 7 (p. 1: "develop an OTA FL algorithm based on a Bayesian approach for signal aggregation"). Quantitative simulation results exist (Figs. 1-6, pp. 9-11), so code results would not apply. PDF matches the DOI: page 1 holds the title "Federated Learning from Heterogeneous Data via Controlled Air Aggregation with Bayesian Estimation" and "Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TSP.2024.3351469".
